questions.text:
Suppose [latex]X_{i}[/latex] for i =1,2,3 are independent and identically distributed random variables whose probability mass functions are [latex]Pr[X_{i}=0]=Pr[X_{i}=1]=1/2[/latex] for i=1,2,3. Define another random variable [latex]Y=X_{1}X_{2}\oplus X_{3}, \; where \; \oplus[/latex] denotes XOR. Then
[latex]Pr[Y=0|X_{3}=0]=[/latex]_______________.
questions.solution:
If [latex]X_3=0[/latex], then [latex]Y=X_1X_2[/latex]. Y = 0 unless both are 1.

P = 1 [latex]-[/latex] 1/4 = 0.75

Answer: 0.75

questions.text: Let R be a relation on the set of ordered pairs of positive integers such that [latex]((p,q),(r,s)) \in R[/latex] if and only if [latex]p-s=q-r[/latex]. Which one of the following is true about R?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Reflexive needs p [latex]-[/latex] q = q [latex]-[/latex] p, i.e. p = q. Fails for (1, 2) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not reflexive.
- Symmetric: ((r,s),(p,q)) needs r [latex]-[/latex] q = s [latex]-[/latex] p, which rearranges to p [latex]-[/latex] s = q [latex]-[/latex] r [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] symmetric.

Answer: Not reflexive but symmetric

questions.text:
In a room there are only two types of people, namely Type 1 and Type 2. Type 1 people always tell the truth and Type 2 people always lie. You give a fair coin to a person in that room, without knowing which type he is from and tell him to toss it and hide the result from you till you ask for it. Upon asking, the person replies the following

"The result of the toss is head if and only if I am telling the truth."

Which of the following options is correct?
questions.solution:
Let H = "result is head".

- Type 1 (truthful): the statement is true and he is telling the truth, so H [latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] True gives H.
- Type 2 (liar): the statement is false and he is not telling the truth. "H [latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] False" is false only when H is true.

Either way the result is head.

Answer: The result is head

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: If the person is of Type 2, then the result is tail
If the person is of Type 1, then the result is tail

questions.text: The number of 4 digit numbers having their digits in non-decreasing order (from left to right) constructed by using the digits belonging to the set {1, 2, 3} is____________.
questions.solution:
A non-decreasing number is fixed once we know how many 1s, 2s and 3s it has. So count solutions of a + b + c = 4 with [latex]a,b,c\ge0[/latex]:

[latex]\binom{4+2}{2}=15[/latex]

Answer: 15

questions.text: Suppose U is the power set of the set S={1,2,3,4,5,6}. For any T[latex]\in[/latex]U, let |T| denote the number of elements in T and T' denote the complement of T. For any T,R[latex]\in[/latex]U, let T\R be the set of all elements in T which are not in R. Which one of the following is true?
questions.solution:
[latex]X\setminus Y=X\cap Y'[/latex] and [latex]Y'\setminus X'=Y'\cap X[/latex]. These are the same set for every X, Y.

- Option 1 fails for X = {1}.
- Option 2: two 5-element subsets of a 6-element set must overlap.
- Option 3 is not true for all X, Y.

Answer: [latex]\forall X\,\forall Y\,(X\setminus Y=Y'\setminus X')[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: [latex]\exists X\in U \; \exists Y\in U \; [/latex] [latex](|X|=5,\; |Y|=5 \; and \;  X \cap  Y=\phi )[/latex]
[latex]\forall X\in U \; \forall Y\in U \;[/latex] [latex] (|X|=2,\; |Y|=3 \; and \; X \setminus  Y=\phi )[/latex]
[latex]\forall X \in U \; \forall Y\in U\; (X \setminus  Y=Y' \setminus  X')[/latex]
